cohort: 784 women with singleton pregnancies who had live-born deliveries after either fresh or frozen embryo transfer between January 2007 and December 2018.
finding: Singletons born following frozen embryo transfer (FET) had significantly higher birth weight, were born later, and had a lower incidence of preterm birth compared to those born following fresh embryo transfer (fresh ET).
birth_weight: FET group: 3137 g (2880-3441 g); Fresh ET group: 3060 g (2710-3340 g)
gest_age: FET group: 39.0 weeks (38.0-40.0 weeks); Fresh ET group: 38.0 weeks (37.0-39.0 weeks)
